summary: Pi-based settings and credential storage APIs persist updates under OS locks, preserve other records and access controls, and distinguish committed durability errors. Linux native gates, native Windows workspace checks, and Intel macOS native gates pass. The initial full Linux preflight had 30 passing gates and one Rust lint failure, fixed and verified by the native rerun. Counts in preflight commands are gates; Cargo commands count test cases, including doctests. No runtime caller wires the writes yet, so scope 05 remains open.

results.behavior: Restart reads, stale independent writers, unknown/OAuth record preservation, runtime-key exclusion, malformed-file refusal, failure cleanup, committed error state, ACL and read-only checks. Four writer subprocesses synchronize on stdin and preserve all 120 updates; a killed holder releases its OS lock.
Rust formatting, Clippy, workspace tests and build, native PTY scenarios and keyless evals. Linux PTY: 22 pass. Intel macOS PTY: 20 pass, 2 Linux /proc-specific skips.
The initial Linux full preflight passed 30 gates and failed Rust Clippy on an unused binding. The native rerun passed after its removal; the unchanged non-native gates were not repeated.

missingEvidence.reason: Writes are synchronous. Async callers must own blocking work, cancellation and teardown; project settings/trust and OAuth flows remain outside this slice.

missingEvidence.what: Power-loss, network-filesystem and full security-metadata qualification
missingEvidence.reason: Tests cover process locks, killed holders and injected write/flush failures, not physical power loss. Newly created ancestor directories are not synced. Windows has no directory fsync. Metadata limitations are documented in json_store; Apple Silicon was not tested.
The separate scope 04 ACL sandbox failed deletion/move confinement and stays unavailable by default; passing storage tests do not close it.
